### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**9** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 47 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e1311d1603b3722f9d23abf92f926ca3fee6659` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5f1ee24787bf006f9bc69a1238e2f819d5593e45` — the merge of head `6c9a7c5d5df03309d6062dc81aa1098ff02e32e4` into base `0e1311d1603b3722f9d23abf92f926ca3fee6659`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5f1ee24787bf006f9bc69a1238e2f819d5593e45 && git checkout 5f1ee24787bf006f9bc69a1238e2f819d5593e45
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0e1311d1603b3722f9d23abf92f926ca3fee6659 6c9a7c5d5df03309d6062dc81aa1098ff02e32e4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0e1311d1603b3722f9d23abf92f926ca3fee6659 && git merge --no-ff 6c9a7c5d5df03309d6062dc81aa1098ff02e32e4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e1311d1603b3722f9d23abf92f926ca3fee6659
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `947b85b8ac97c38bd95cc869b1db5649230d86ee`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/ai-service-auto-inject.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/ai-service-auto-inject.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-plugins.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ai-auto-inject-refusal.test.ts + packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/unmapped-columns.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/json-stdout.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/plugin-detection.ts, packages/cli/src/index.ts, packages/cli/package.json, packages/cli/test/serve-optional-plugin-intent.test.ts, packages/core/src/stack-auth.ts, packages/core/src/capability-composition.ts, packages/core/src/kernel.ts, packages/core/src/plugin-loader.ts, packages/types/src/node.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx (the changeset `.changeset/31411-migrate-refuses-serve-only-ai-plugin.md` is the prose face, read for ② and for agreement with the code)

Inputs read: card #31411 body and all four comments (ruling 6718342541, triage 6718464157, claim 6718620169, os-dev-report 6719578653); PR #31446 body, file list, commits and the net diff `origin/main...pr/31446` at this head; `main` at `0e1311d1` for serve's inline rule, `composeServedPlatform` and every caller; the 53 check-runs on this head. The PR's current head is `6c9a7c5d` (one commit on top: the changeset level `minor` to `patch`, nothing else); this record names `947b85b8` as the brief asked, and the one difference is judged in ②.

### ① Derived judgments

**Who refuses, and on what.** `composeServedPlatform` has one call site (`buildSchemaMigrationPlugins`, reached only with `servedPlatform` set), and `bootSchemaStack` passes `composeServedPlatform: true` from exactly four commands on main: `os migrate plan` (plan.ts 227), `os migrate apply` (apply.ts 234), `os migrate unmapped-columns` (unmapped-columns.ts 299) and the organization-ownership ceremony's `--apply` boot (organization-ownership.ts 732). The ceremony's plan-face boot (line 513) composes nothing and is unaffected; `security-catalog-overlays` and `packageless-overlays` compose the host stack without the served platform and are unaffected. The changeset names exactly those four. A project with neither a config file nor a compiled artifact returns `NOTHING_COMPOSED` before the predicate runs; an unloadable host config is refused on its own terms (#12953) and never reaches it.

The refused set is: predicate not `off` AND no plugin in `[...basePlugins, ...hostPlugins, ...composed]` named `com.objectstack.service-ai` or of class `AIServicePlugin`. Predicate inputs, as the diff reads them: `requires` is the pre-existing shared rule (a host config's own declared tokens; otherwise the compiled artifact's when it declares any; otherwise the config's) — `ai` or `ai-studio` present ⇒ `required`; else the host's `package.json` (the config's directory, else cwd) declaring `@objectstack/service-ai` or `@objectstack/service-ai-studio` ⇒ `auto`; the `ai` tier (declared `tiers`, else the preset's default `core, i18n, ui, ai, auth`, plus the tier of each declared token) off ⇒ `off`, no refusal. So: `requires: ['ai']` or `['ai-studio']` without a mounted AI plugin is refused whatever `tiers` says (both tokens open the `ai` tier, `CAPABILITY_TO_TIER`); a dependency-only config is refused unless `tiers` omits `ai`; a config that mounts the plugin (instance, or a string specifier both boots materialize) is never refused; a config with no AI intent is never refused.

**Serve's boot decision is byte-identical.** `Serve.resolveOptionalPluginLoad` keeps its signature and delegates to `resolveOptionalPluginLoad`, whose four lines are the old body verbatim; the Studio decision still calls the static. `resolveAiServiceLoad` composes the same three expressions serve had inline — `has('ai') || has('ai-studio')`, `hostDeclares(service-ai) || hostDeclares(service-ai-studio)`, `tierEnabled('ai')` — and serve now passes `declaredRequires` (still `served.declared`), `tierEnabled('ai')` (still from `resolveStackTiers` over the full served token list with `flags.preset ?? 'default'`) and the same `isDeclaredByHost(pkg, servedAppRootOrCwd())` closure. `mountsAiServicePlugin(plugins)` is the old `.some` by registered name or class name. The 40-case oracle test (5 `requires` spellings × tier on/off × 4 declared-dependency states, the oracle being the old inline reading) covers the whole input product, and `test/serve-optional-plugin-intent.test.ts` still pins the static. `required` / `auto` / `off`, `ai` and `ai-studio`, dependency present or not, plugin mounted or not: every arm resolves as before.

**One predicate, no surviving inline copy.** On the PR tree the base-AI rule's tokens (`has('ai')`, the two package names, `com.objectstack.service-ai`, `AIServicePlugin`) occur in `packages/cli/src` only in the util, its test, and the test fixture. What serve.ts still carries is the Studio rule (`declaredRequires.has('ai-studio')`, `com.objectstack.service-ai-studio`, `AIStudioPlugin`) — a different question (does serve load Studio once the base loaded), not a copy of the base rule; the util's docstring states that the base's answer is the whole answer. The source pins in the new test guard both files against a restatement.

**Tier and root parity, judged on the inputs.** Serve feeds `resolveStackTiers` the full served token list (declared + `email` + `mcp`/`pinyin-search` host defaults + the always-on slate + `job`/`queue`); the composition feeds it the declared tokens. `CAPABILITY_TO_TIER` maps only `ai`, `ai-studio`, `i18n`, `ui`, `auth`, so no appended token can open `ai`: `has('ai')` is equal for every config. The composition passes `serveFlags.preset` when given (no caller sets it) and `resolveStackTiers` falls back to `default`, as serve's `flags.preset ?? 'default'` does. The only divergence is an operator who serves with `--preset minimal` (tiers `core` only, serve injects nothing): the migrate commands cannot know serve's flags — the same documented limitation the pre-existing auth gate has ("these commands take no preset"). Dependency root: serve anchors at the config's directory (#11185), the composition at `dirname(hostConfigPath)`, cwd only when there is no config; both read the same manifest through `readHostDeclaration`.

**Public surface.** `@objectstack/cli`'s exports map is `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`, `./package.json`; `src/index.ts` re-exports command classes only. `src/utils/ai-service-auto-inject.ts` and its five exports are unreachable from outside the package: internal. `ServeCommand.resolveOptionalPluginLoad` keeps its signature and semantics. No published name is added, removed or re-shaped.

### ② Semver level

- **Level.** At this head the changeset grades `@objectstack/cli` `minor` under `Metadata-protocol: none`. Under maintainer ruling A (#25105) `none` ⇒ `patch`; `Check Changeset` is red on this head for exactly that and nothing else (both runs, 42463012352 and 42465373877, same text). The dispatch order's `minor` was the seat's error, ruled already; the dev moved the entry to `patch` in `6c9a7c5d` (the PR's current head, the only change since this one). **should-fix, satisfied on the next head** — not a FAIL here per the seat's ruling. The landing record must name the head that lands, so this record will not carry `6c9a7c5d`.
- **BREAKING section.** Present with Why / Before / Now / Who moves / Unchanged, and each claim agrees with the code: `plan` / `apply` catch the thrown `Error` and answer `{ error: message }` on `--json` with `this.exit(1)` (plan.ts 235, apply.ts 241); the ceremony answers `error: boot_failed, reason: boot-failed, detail` with exit 1 (`refuse`, organization-ownership.ts 407-419); the text names the reason (`requires` token or `package.json`) and the remedy. "Unchanged" (mounted plugin plans as today; `ai` tier off plans as today; no AI intent plans as today; serve loads the same plugins) holds by ①. Nothing an author writes is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO map is owed; the one-line fix ("add the plugin to `plugins`") is stated.
- **Clause-② arm.** `no (narrowing)` is right: the exported names are internal (①), so no exported widening makes it `yes (narrowing)`.
- **ADR-0087 disposition.** `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is in the gate's closed vocabulary (`CATEGORIES`, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs) and honest: no key, export or stored shape moves, the body carries no migration prescription (the "Remedy" is a config edit, not a rewrite of anything at rest). The gate ran green in `Lint & Repo Gates` on this head.
- **Skills-docs line.** The `skills/**` half holds: `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` names `AIServicePlugin` as cloud / EE, reverse-mounted by a cloud host (line 286), and its line 331 teaches the generic required-vs-best-effort rule naming no AI; `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` names `service-ai` as cloud / EE. The `content/docs/` half is literally true (no page describes the migrate composition's AI handling), with one nuance: `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` line 612 does document that serve auto-registers the services `requires` names, `ai` included, and its `os migrate plan` / `apply` section lists that command's refusals and warnings without this new one. `Flag docs affected by code changes` is green. **nit**: a line in that migrate section naming the refusal and the remedy would close it; the refusal text carries the remedy itself and the measured reach is zero hosts.

### ③ Boundary flags

Report 6719578653 lists `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. Its three notes, and the PR body's, answered:

1. **The `auto` case (dependency declared, nothing in `requires`) is refused too.** Answered, accepted. Serve attempts the inject for `auto` as well; `loadOptionalServicePlugin` with `required: false` warns and continues only when the import fails, i.e. a package declared in `package.json` but not installed (or exporting no plugin) — a broken install, in which the remedy's explicit mount would fail at import too. For a declared-and-installed dependency serve boots WITH the AI tables and a plan without them is the defect the card names. The maintainer's condition names "the host-declared dependency" as an input, so refusing on it is inside the ruling. nit: the `auto` refusal text could say serve loads it best-effort, so an operator with a deliberately uninstalled dependency understands why.
2. **`unmapped-columns` inherits the refusal.** Verified (unmapped-columns.ts 298-299). Its catch answers `{ error: 'boot_failed', detail }` with exit 1 — a different JSON shape from `plan` / `apply`, but that command's own pre-existing shape for every boot failure, not this PR's. The changeset names the command.
3. **`bootSchemaStack` releases stdout on a composition throw.** Verified. The release closure is idempotent (`realStdoutWrite !== original` guard; it restores the stream only if still its own), the success path releases only in `shutdown()`, so the two never both fire; `emitJson` writes through `writeStdoutDirect`, which reaches the real stream with or without a reservation, so the command's own `{ error }` answer is unaffected either way. Throws from `createStandaloneStack`, `kernel.use` of the stack plugins or `runtime.start()` after the reservation still leak it — pre-existing and not widened by this PR, out of this card. nit / follow-up.
4. **Serial.** #31377 (serve.ts comments) merged 06:50Z before the claim; the branch merged `origin/main` at `1fdc501e`; the diff carries no conflict residue in serve.ts.
5. **"`requires: ['ai']` always opens the `ai` tier, so the tier-off control uses a declared dependency."** Correct by `CAPABILITY_TO_TIER`; the control (`tiers: ['core','i18n','ui','auth']` plus the dependency) is the only configuration in which the tier can deny the intent.
6. **Escalated to nothing.** No flag needs the maintainer.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Another spelling, a bundle, a preset.** `mountsAiServicePlugin` is serve's own mounted-check verbatim (registered name or class name), so the composition has exactly serve's blind spots and no others: a string specifier `'@objectstack/service-ai'` in `plugins` is materialized by both boots and seen; a bundle becomes an `AppPlugin`, not an AI plugin, in both; a preset is a tier list, never a plugin; a plugin that nests a `kernel.use` from its `init` cannot register after bootstrap in either boot. The declaration Proxy preserves `name` and `constructor`, and the raw host instances are in the list as well. No config was found that serve boots with AI and the composition refuses, except for the `--preset minimal` flag case in ①. nit (pre-existing, shared with the auth gate).
- **Dependency-only.** Judged in ③-1: a false refusal only on a broken install. nit.
- **Tier read at migrate time vs serve time.** Same rule (`resolveStackTiers`), inputs analysed in ①, `has('ai')` provably equal for every config; the flag-time divergence is unknowable to a separate command and documented. nit.
- **Cloud host path.** The cloud host mounts `AIServicePlugin` explicitly since cloud#3744; its host config holds the instance, `isHostConfig` is true (plugins with `init`), the instance is in `hostPlugins`, so the predicate's `required` / `auto` answer is moot and nothing is refused. The control-plane host that ships no Studio (cloud#107) is untouched: the Studio half is not part of the predicate.
- **Exit code and message vs the existing migrate refusals.** The thrown plain `Error` takes the same catch as the composition's existing throw (`Capability "x": pkg did not export …`) and the #12953 unloadable-config refusal: `plan` / `apply` `{ error }` + exit 1, the ceremony `boot_failed` + `reason: boot-failed` + `detail` + exit 1, `unmapped-columns` `boot_failed` + `detail` + exit 1. The message names the reason and the remedy; it carries no `errorCodeFields` code, like the other plain-Error boot refusals. nit: none owed.
- **Refusal before any write.** `kernel.use` only validates and stores the plugin (`PluginLoader.loadPlugin`); `init` runs at `runtime.start()`, which comes after `buildSchemaMigrationPlugins` resolves. The refusal fires inside `composeServedPlatform`, before the auth family, before any provider is imported or constructed, before the composition's plugins are registered, before `start()`. `resolveStandaloneDatabase` and `apply`'s occupancy probe before it read only; the ceremony's `--apply` refuses at its boot before the plan file is compared. No write precedes it.
- **stdout reservation.** No leak on a composition throw, no double release (③-3).
- **Ceremony plan face.** Only the `--apply` boot composes the served platform; the plan face never claimed parity with serve and composes no host stack, so "plan succeeds, apply refuses" on such a config is the pre-existing division of that command, consistent with the card's wording ("the paths that compose through `composeServedPlatform`"). Noted, no finding.
- **AI Studio.** A config that mounts the base plugin explicitly and relies on serve to auto-inject `@objectstack/service-ai-studio` is not refused; the base's answer is the predicate's whole answer, as its docstring says. Studio is cloud-private and outside this card (which names `@objectstack/service-ai`); whether Studio declares tables of its own is a cloud question. nit / follow-up for the cloud seat.
- **The oracle.** `serveBefore` in the predicate test is the old inline reading in shape; 40 cases exhaust requires × tier × dependency. The migrate test runs the real commands against a temp project and SQLite file with three refusals and three controls, and the refusal condition is the one the dev ablated to red.

Findings: should-fix ×1 (changeset level `minor` → `patch` on this head; moved in `6c9a7c5d`); nits ×5 (`auto` refusal text, cli.mdx migrate section, other post-reservation throws, `--preset minimal` unknowable, Studio follow-up). No must-fix.
